each of diagnostic methods (x-ray, bronchoscoopy, cytological examination) used to asses the tumor response to the treatment in patients with small cell lung cancer yields independent information correlated with the survival risk of a particular patient.
the response to the treatment in limited small cell lung caner is related to the survival of patients and is dependent on the method of its assessment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the value of diagnostic methods in assessing the tumor response to treatment.
the value of diagnostic methods in assessing response to treatment in SCLC.
the value of the methods used to assess tumor response to treatment in small cell lung carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
each of the diagnostic methods used in this study yields independent information on the survival time of patients.
all 3 diagnostic methods should be used in the assessment of tumor response in patients with small cell lung cancer.
the response to treatment of small cell lung carcinoma should be assessed by all 3 methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a patient's response to the treatment should be evaluated by a combination of radiological, cytological and bronchoscopic examinations.
a comprehensive assessment of tumor response to treatment of patients with small cell lung cancer is necessary to evaluate the treatment effectiveness and survival risk of patients.
the response criteria must be defined in terms of all 3 methods.

the response assessment in patients with limited SCLC must be based on all of these methods.
the response to treatment must be assessed by all available methods and not only radiologically, because it is a main prognostic factor for the patients with small cell lung carcinoma.
the assessment of the response to treatment should be based on all 3 methods of evaluation.
